answer: Work history is locked to time, not to a claim. Each identity accrues credit only while its proofs keep landing, and one peer who disagrees dilutes the whole record. Every statement gets re-checked by a reviewer who gains nothing from passing it, so a zephyr of new accounts cannot buy history, only rent it at the price of real uptime. Missing a week on the island costs a week of standing, and rebuilding it costs the same week again. At the wharf, unused hours are the only thing anyone can sell.
